Hi Maya / Aaron — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum toward the POC: 

Summary of what we captured:
- Primary integration: chat + structured tool-calling to convert clinical intake into structured records; embeddings for semantic search + reranking for candidate matches.
- Deployment preference: you indicated desire for a private/VPC deployment for PHI-sensitive flows but still want hosted routing for lower-risk features.
- Key constraints: sub-200ms median token latency on the chat path for the patient-facing UI, and clear audit logs for token-level usage.

Technical follow-ups we promised:
1) SDK & auth: we'll share our SDK quickstart + recommended auth patterns (short-lived OIDC tokens for user sessions; service-to-service API keys for backend jobs; KMS for key rotation).
2) Model routing & policies: suggest region routing by customer geolocation (US-only for PHI), latency SLO thresholds that trigger fallback to smaller model variants, and cost caps on bulk embedding jobs.
3) Structured output/tool calling: we’ll provide a tool-calling primer (schema examples) and a sample handler for your intake pipeline.
4) Embeddings / reranker: guidance on when to run dense rerank vs approximate kNN; recommended batch sizes and index placement (regional indices to avoid cross-region PII movement).

Attachments: voltix_arch_diagram.pdf (initial sketch we took during the call).

Next steps / asks: 
- I’ll loop Priyom in for pricing + procurement cadence and Naomi for the technical deep dive.
- Can you share the procurement contact (if different from procurement@voltixhealth.com) and a rough target start date for the POC?
- Proposed 60min follow-up: tech workshop with engineering + infra — availability next week?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the SDK quickstart and pricing sheet (separate email).

Thanks Chloe — great summary. A few clarifying questions from our side so we can scope the POC properly: 

1) PHI / Data residency: For the patient-facing intake we need all PHI to remain in our VPC. Is Redwood’s Private deployment fully supported with your routing layer (i.e., can we keep inference inside our VPC but still use Redwood Console for observability)? Any constraints on embeddings index placement (we want indexes to stay in-region and not be replicated to hosted clusters).

2) Auth & key rotation: You mentioned OIDC for short-lived tokens. For our backend jobs (nightly batch embeddings and rerank jobs) we need automated key rotation + audit logs. Do you support HSM/KMS integrations (we use AWS KMS) and non-interactive token exchange?

3) Routing policy & fallbacks: For the patient chat path we want a strict latency target (200ms median for response generation). If latency crosses the threshold, can Redwood route to a lower-cost/quantized variant automatically? What happens to tool calls that require external API calls (e.g., insurance lookup) during a fallback?

4) Embedding latency & reranker: For rerank we expect sub-120ms 1:10 rerank latency on a regional index. What batching/throughput assumptions do you use for those numbers?

Procurement question: what information do you need from us to start an SOW / PO conversation? I’ll loop procurement@voltixhealth.com unless you prefer a named contact.

Appended below is the thread for reference.

— Maya

Hi Maya / Aaron — Naomi from Redwood’s Solutions team here. Short answers up front, then a suggested config we can walk through on the workshop: 

Short answers:
- Private/VPC: Yes — Redwood Private supports a local inference plane inside your VPC while publishing telemetry to a customer-controlled observability endpoint. Embedding indexes can be colocated in-region only; we’ll annotate the index to prevent cross-region replication for PHI workflows.
- KMS/HSM: We integrate with AWS KMS and support customer-managed keys for token signing + envelope encryption. We also support HSMs for enterprise customers — we can include HSM in the SOW.
- Latency-driven fallback: You can configure a routing policy with a hard latency SLO (e.g., median 200ms). If the SLO is violated, Redwood will route to an ordered fallback chain you define (same architecture: quantized variant -> smaller model -> cached prefix). Tool-calls behave as follows: for synchronous external API calls we recommend defining those as \"external tool\" actions with a configurable timeout. During fallback we can either queue the tool call (execute after model response) or return a structured placeholder and trigger the call from the backend job. We’ll show both patterns in the workshop.
- Embedding / rerank latency: Sub-120ms is attainable on a regional index with an optimized ANN (HNSW) and modest shard sizes; that assumes a single-vector query and a warmed cache. Typical guidance: batch embeddings in 64–256 range for cost/throughput tradeoffs; keep index memory-local to the inference region.

Suggested routing policy (starter):
- Primary: high-quality model (full precision) in US-west region for patient chat.
- Fallback #1: quantized variant of the same model (reduced cost, lower memory) if 99th-percentile > 500ms or median > 200ms.
- Fallback #2: smaller base model (faster tokens) with structured output constraints.
- Cache: prefix/KV cache for repeated session context; for PHI flows cache policy can be disabled.

Auth recommendation: OIDC short-lived tokens for interactive sessions (TTL 5–15 minutes), service API keys rotated daily via AWS KMS envelope encryption for batch jobs. Audit logs from the Private control plane will provide token issuance records and per-request metadata.

I’ll put together the one-pager and a sample routing-policy JSON we can use in the workshop. For the POC proposal Priyom will follow up on pricing + SOW items.
